items.html:
The saved data supports upstream parity, author-reference agreement, thermal invariants/convergence, and a narrow EBCM high-precision cancellation check. These should remain separate accuracy concepts.

  1. thermal-result.json contains the fullest thermal qualification: 300 frequencies, 52 upstream comparisons, three angular cuts, 22 convergence records. complete=true; summary.passed=true.

    • rows[] keys: index, frequency_hz, author_absorption_um_squared, rust_absorption_um_squared, rust_seconds, author_relative_error; 52 rows additionally contain upstream_absorption_um_squared, upstream_seconds, upstream_relative_error, upstream_author_relative_error.
    • Author-reference relative error: median 1.917258459e-7, maximum 0.005766535419 at index 3 / 3.113116944 THz. Author absorption 0.00019057008466 μm²; Rust 0.000189471155517 μm².
    • Upstream relative difference: median 1.323991743e-7, maximum 0.000295791054 at index 0 / 3 THz.
    • angular_cuts[]: index, rust_values (200 values), author_max_relative_error, azimuth_invariance_relative_error, helicity_symmetry_relative_error. At indices 164/187/220, author errors are 2.173501520e-7 / 5.790365532e-8 / 6.138131823e-8. Maximum saved symmetry error 1.558360485e-14.
    • convergence[]: index, lmax, absorption_um_squared. Index 0 has lmax 6/8/10/12/14/16; indices 164/187/220/299 have 6/8/10/12. Relative lmax-10 changes against each highest saved order are 5.695067881e-4 / 4.108733256e-4 / 1.858349840e-4 / 2.599787217e-4 / 2.176360404e-4. These are truncation comparisons, not certified errors against exact values.
    • summary also records finite_nonnegative_absorption=true, paper_relative_tolerance=0.01, paper_agreement=true.
    • Native fingerprint 3fea483…; lmax 10; four spheres, radius 2.5e-7 m, spacing 5.2e-7 m, 500 K, helicity polarization. Explicit timing_note: qualification wall times are not isolated performance benchmarks.

  2. thermal-upstream-comparison.json is a different native build, fingerprint a9b550e…, with 52 sampled rows, three angular cuts and 12 convergence records.

    • Same row schema; upstream version 0.4.5.
    • Maximum author relative error 0.005449487248; maximum upstream relative difference 0.000859854501; maximum angular author relative error 4.664861376e-7.
    • Its upstream values are reused explicitly by thermal-result.json through upstream_reference_path and upstream_reference_sha256. Keep the two Rust result sets distinct.
    • Supports upstream parity and sampled author-reference agreement; it contains no thermal high-precision oracle.

  3. thermal-source.json embeds the reference arrays needed for accuracy plots.

    • frequencies_hz, wavenumbers_cm_inverse, absorption_um_squared, thermal_energy_j_per_m3_per_cm_inverse: 300 values each.
    • polar_angles: 200 values; angular_cut_frequency_indices: [164,187,220]; angular_photons_per_second_per_cm_inverse: 200 × 3.
    • material: 346 × 3, identified by material_columns=["frequency_hz","epsilon_real","epsilon_imag"].
    • Provenance: DOI 10.1103/41m5-9ztm, author repository, commit ec710fc…, archive/notebook/file hashes.
    • Recorded source notes: angular cuts equal saved author columns exactly; values already include 200π conversion; executable source uses T†T despite different notebook markdown.
    • No external NPY/NPZ arrays are referenced by these thermal JSON files. Numerical arrays are embedded.

  4. ebcm-l6-cancellation.json provides eight selected matrix-entry checks against analytic zero, supported by 80-digit mpmath.

    • Top-level keys: native_profile, mpmath_digits, symmetry, results.
    • Row keys: out, in, analytic_value, mpmath_absolute_value, mpmath_reflection_error, integral_of_absolute_integrand, epsilon_times_absolute_integral, upstream_default, upstream_tight, quadrature_warnings, native_by_quadrature_order.
    • Symmetry states that for m=0, odd l_out+l_in, this equatorially symmetric surface has an odd reflected integrand. Every analytic_value is zero.
    • Example out [1,0,1], in [6,0,1]: mpmath magnitude 5.912810312e-82; double-precision roundoff scale epsilon_times_absolute_integral 1.623879056e-10. Upstream magnitude 6.604102586e-10; native magnitudes at q 48/96/192 are 3.936608724e-10 / 1.633188329e-10 / 2.082177126e-10.
    • All eight upstream default/tight values are identical; every row records a roundoff warning.
    • Plot absolute residuals, not relative error against zero. The orders demonstrate cancellation/roundoff behavior, not monotonic convergence. Scope is eight selected entries; this artifact lacks source/native hashes and does not establish whole-matrix accuracy.

  5. Existing thermal-qualification.png and thermal-qualification.svg are present. qualification.json contains ebeam/cpc, not thermal. ebcm-l3-q96.json and ebcm-l4-q96.json contain timing/RSS metadata, no saved numerical error results.

Verified by file listing and lightweight JSON parsing only. No edits, rendering, builds, tests, benchmarks or Git changes.

items.html:
• P2 — Metric-name heuristic misclassifies raw and scaled residuals. plot_benchmarks.py:1114 treats only names containing absolute or _abs_ as raw errors. Paper metrics passivity_nonnegative_violation and scattering_exceeds_extinction are unnormalized differences (qualify_paper_accuracy.py:261); their workloads use 1/eV, 1/(eV nm), efficiency and power fraction. The renderer pools them and labels them dimensionless at line 1145. Conversely, layer_split_scaled_absolute, divergence_scaled_absolute and ewald_split_scaled_absolute are normalized by a reference scale (qualify_physics.py:147, lines 270–277 and 606–607), but receive the “raw workload units” label at line 1137.

  • P3 — Measured high-precision residuals are shown as “not measured.” plot_benchmarks.py:1215 uses that label whenever error is null. The frozen reference collector deliberately emits error=null plus error_high_precision when a measured residual cannot survive JSON float64 conversion (qualify_references.py:325, lines 437–450). Its small-argument/high-order spherical-Bessel grid exercises underflow-scale references. The precise value survives in expanded details, but the primary table incorrectly describes it as absent.

Source and saved-unit inspection only; no edits or execution of collectors, plots, tests or benchmarks.

items.html:
All three sampling metrics aggregate CPU and CUDA checks; only the fused-field and phase-probe residuals are GPU-specific.

Raw metric Exact meaning Saved gate
Sampling max_abs_error Maximum complex component error across cached CPU column/row layouts, prepared-fused CPU, and CUDA cold/resident/roundtrip outputs against native plane::field Each component was checked against 2e-12 × (1 + abs(reference_component)); reference magnitudes are not saved, so the aggregate remains an absolute-error diagnostic
Sampling max_adjoint_abs_error Maximum coefficient-gradient component error across CPU row layout and CUDA adjoints against CPU column-layout Fᴴg Same componentwise gate; reference magnitudes unavailable
Sampling max_adjoint_normalized_pairing_error Maximum over CPU and CUDA adjoint checks of abs(gᴴ(Fc) − gradientᴴc) / max(1, norm(g) × norm(Fc)) 2e-12
Fields max_abs_error Maximum complex component difference between production CUDA PlaneWaves.evaluate and native CPU plane::field 2e-12 × (1 + max(abs(reference))); reference_scale is calculated but omitted from JSON
Field-phases max_abs_error Maximum complex component difference between the selected diagnostic CUDA kernel variant and native CPU plane::field Componentwise 2e-12 × (1 + abs(reference_component)); scale omitted

Source anchors:

  • benchmark_sampling.rs:145: absolute and pairing formulas. Forward aggregation starts at line 346; adjoint aggregation at 363; measured-loop CPU/CUDA aggregation at 391–460.
  • qualify_plane.rs:90: separate prepared-CPU check, GPU-only reported residual, unsaved reference scale.
  • probe_plane.rs:488: reported residual for the selected diagnostic kernel.

The sampling scope is fixed-operator coefficient derivatives only. Its three errors are aggregate maxima across initial checks and changing coefficient/cotangent applications; samples[] contains timing values only, with no per-application error values.

Available schemas:

  • Sampling raw JSON emits the three metrics directly, plus points, modes, operator_shape, precision, scope, adjoint_scope and timing samples. It has no schema, workload, explicit accuracy status, per-backend error split, or saved reference scale.
  • Fields raw JSON identifies workload="weighted-plane-fields" and emits max_abs_error, lossless, points/modes and timing/memory fields.
  • Phase-probe raw JSON emits variant, lossless, real_k_specialized, points/modes, max_abs_error, and timing diagnostics: context_seconds, mode_upload_seconds, point_upload_seconds, output_allocation_seconds, cold_kernel_seconds, warm_kernel_seconds, download_seconds, plus both CPU timings. Wrapper execution selects variant 3; this is explicitly a diagnostic mirror rather than the production API.
  • benchmark_gpu.py:258 wraps these in schema_version=1, kind="gpu", parameters.workload, source, environment, normalized timing results, and unchanged raw. check_returncode() precedes wrapper serialization: failed Rust assertions/checks produce no successful wrapper result.
  • No exactmax fields occur in these three current Rust emitters or the inspected phase JSONL artifacts. No mathematical exact-value reference is recorded.

Saved examples:

  • final-sampling-p16384-m512-t4.json: forward absolute 1.148198255e-16, adjoint absolute 1.063444294e-14, normalized pairing 2.632972040e-17.
  • final-m64-p16384-t32.json: production-field GPU absolute error 3.376611507e-16.
  • probe-m64-p16384-t16.jsonl: three legacy diagnostic variants 0/1/2, errors 3.402181501e-16 / 3.402181501e-16 / 1.943200040e-16. These older rows omit real_k_specialized.
  • fma-m1024-p262144-v3-t32.jsonl: variant 3, real_k_specialized=false, absolute error 8.934853795e-17.

Read-only source and saved-JSON inspection; no edits or numerical execution.

Minimum case envelope:

{
    "kind": "accuracy",
    "id": "wigner-axis",
    "suite": "test",
    "fingerprint": "test",
    "raw": {"observations": rows},
}

Each of three rows needs:

{
    "family": "wigner_rotation",
    "backend": "treams-rs",
    "reference_kind": "high_precision",
    "metric": "max_scaled_error",
    "error": error,
    "parameters": {"degree": degree},
    "selection": "post_failure_diagnostic",
    "tolerance": 1.0,
    "status": "failed" if error > 1 else "passed",
}

Use (degree, error) values (23, 0.0), (24, 0.5), (25, 2.0). selection, tolerance, and status are optional mechanically, but match the collector’s semantics.

Pitfalls:

  • Capture the save whose name starts with high-order-; plot_accuracy also emits a two-axis distribution figure.
  • Omit series and x to avoid an additional convergence plot. No observation id is required by this plotting path.
  • Assert the captured single axis has linear x scale, ticks exactly [23, 24, 25], and nonnegative lower bounds. Including zero error exercises the y-axis boundary.
  • Current inspected source still calls set_xscale("symlog", linthresh=1) at line 2075; the fixture should fail that implementation.
